counters.label: Doomsday Clock
counters.trendLabel: 4 s closer than 2025 (89 s); closest ever
counters.note: A symbolic setting by the Bulletin's Science and Security Board, not a measurement or a probability.

counters.label: Nuclear warheads
counters.trendLabel: 9,745 military stockpile · 4,012 deployed. Was 12,241 a year earlier
counters.note: New START expired in February 2026 with no replacement. Inventory is shrinking only because retired warheads are being dismantled; usable stockpiles are growing.

counters.label: Global temperature
counters.note: Anomaly relative to NASA's 1951-1980 baseline, NOT the pre-industrial baseline used for the 1.5 °C target (pre-industrial is cooler by roughly a quarter to a third of a degree, depending on dataset). Window: Oct 2025 to Sep 2026. Latest single month: +1.38 °C.

source.name: NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4)

counters.label: Atmospheric CO₂
counters.note: Mauna Loa monthly mean for Sep 2026. It rises and falls with the seasons (lowest around September), so compare the same month across years. Deseasonalized trend value: 429.6 ppm. Pre-industrial level was about 280 ppm.

counters.label: Global mean sea level
counters.trendLabel: 3.2 mm/yr over the record · 3.7 mm/yr over the last 10 years
counters.basis: Elevated when the last 10 years rise faster than the full record (a comparison of two observed trends, not a forecast)
counters.note: Global mean sea level from satellite altimetry (TOPEX/Poseidon, Jason-1/2/3, Sentinel-6), 66°S to 66°N, annual signal removed, no glacial-isostatic correction. 'Since 1993' compares the latest value with the average of the first year of the record. The source publishes with a delay of many months.
counters.cadence: source updates every few weeks, lags the present

source.name: NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry
source.license: Free; acknowledge 'Altimetry data are provided by NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry'

counters.label: Sea-ice extent
counters.trendLabel: Arctic −21% · Antarctic −10% vs the 1981-2010 mean for this date
counters.basis: Elevated when either pole is 10% or more below its 1981-2010 mean for the date, critical at 20%
counters.note: Extent is the ocean area with at least 15% ice cover, from passive-microwave satellites (NSIDC Sea Ice Index). The latest daily values are preliminary and can be revised. Sea ice floats, so its melt barely changes sea level; it matters for climate feedbacks, ecosystems and shipping. Land ice (glaciers, ice sheets) is what raises sea level.

source.name: NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 (NOAA@NSIDC)
source.license: Free; cite Fetterer et al., Sea Ice Index

counters.label: Glacier ice loss
counters.note: GlaMBIE community estimate combining field, airborne and satellite measurements of all glaciers outside the ice sheets. The loss equals about 0.75 mm of sea-level rise per year. A published figure, not a live feed.

counters.label: Ice-sheet loss
counters.note: IMBIE assessment of Greenland and Antarctica combined; 21.0 ± 1.9 mm of sea-level rise from ice sheets over 1992-2020. A published figure, not a live feed.

source.name: IMBIE Team, Nature 2018 / Earth Syst. Sci. Data 2021

counters.label: Earth Overshoot Day
counters.trendLabel: Humanity used a year of renewable resources by this date
counters.note: Modelled estimate by Global Footprint Network and York University.

counters.label: WHO outbreak reports
counters.basis: Elevated from 12 WHO reports in 90 days
counters.trendLabel: Latest: Pneumonia of undetermined etiology - the Russian Federation
counters.note: Count of WHO Disease Outbreak News publications, not a count of active outbreaks: WHO only publishes events it judges relevant for international attention, and one outbreak can have several reports. On the map, each report is placed at the centre of the country named in its title (not at the outbreak site).

counters.label: Shipping chokepoints
counters.basis: Counted when a chokepoint's 7-day transits are more than 25% below its 12-month average; elevated at one chokepoint, critical at three
counters.note: Average daily ship transits over the last 7 days vs the average of the previous 12 months, per chokepoint. A drop can come from war, weather, drought (Panama), or rerouting; it does not say why. PortWatch publishes with a delay of several days.

source.name: IMF PortWatch (with Oxford University)
source.license: Open data with attribution; verify terms before redistributing raw data

counters.label: Armed conflict in the news
counters.note: Count of news-reported events that GDELT's automatic coding classed as fighting or mass violence involving military or armed groups, or between countries. It measures how much armed conflict is reported, not casualties, and it still contains coding errors and duplicates. Use it for relative hotspots, not for totals.

counters.label: Asteroid close approaches
counters.basis: Elevated when a known object passes within one Moon-distance. No known object is rated a hazard, so it is never critical.
counters.note: Known near-Earth objects passing within 0.05 au (about 19.5 lunar distances, LD). Close approaches are routine and almost always involve small objects; the ones listed are known orbits that do not hit Earth. Diameter ranges are rough estimates from brightness, assuming a reflectivity between 0.05 and 0.25. NASA's Sentry system tracks 2,222 objects with a non-zero computed chance of impact within about a century; 0 of them rate 1 or higher on the Torino scale (0 = no hazard, 10 = certain global catastrophe).

source.name: NASA/JPL Center for Near-Earth Object Studies

counters.label: Geomagnetic activity
counters.basis: Elevated from Kp 5 (NOAA G1 storm), critical from Kp 7 (G3)
counters.note: Planetary Kp index, 0-9, from NOAA SWPC (3-hour values). G1 starts at Kp 5. The 1859 Carrington event is estimated to have been beyond anything in the modern record.

volcanoes.name: Campi Flegrei
volcanoes.levelLabel: Yellow alert level (Italian Civil Protection), unrest ongoing
volcanoes.detail: Ground uplift and earthquake swarms continue. Yellow is the second of four levels and does not mean an eruption is expected.

volcanoes.name: Toba
volcanoes.detail: Monitored locally; this site has no live status for Toba.

volcanoes.name: Aira Caldera (Sakurajima)
volcanoes.detail: Sakurajima is monitored by the Japan Meteorological Agency; this site does not ingest its alert level yet.

dyads.label: United States – Russia
dyads.note: New START expired Feb 2026 with no replacement (SIPRI).
dyads.why: Both states hold nuclear weapons, and they hold the two largest arsenals (SIPRI).

dyads.label: Russia – Ukraine
dyads.note: Nuclear-armed state in a direct war.
dyads.why: Ukraine holds no nuclear weapons. The pair is listed only because a nuclear-armed state is in a direct war with it.

dyads.label: India – Pakistan
dyads.note: Both nuclear-armed; SIPRI 2026 cites the outbreak of conflict between them.

dyads.label: India – China
dyads.why: Both states hold nuclear weapons and share a disputed border.

dyads.label: North Korea – South Korea
dyads.why: South Korea holds no nuclear weapons. The pair is listed because a nuclear-armed state shares a divided border with it.

dyads.label: North Korea – Japan
dyads.why: Japan holds no nuclear weapons. The pair is listed because it lies within range of a nuclear-armed neighbour.

dyads.label: Israel – Iran
dyads.note: Israel is an undeclared nuclear state; Iran is a threshold state, not a nuclear-armed one.
dyads.why: Israel is an undeclared nuclear state. Iran holds no nuclear weapons; it is listed as a threshold state because its enrichment programme is under international scrutiny (IAEA).

dyads.label: United States – Iran
dyads.why: Iran holds no nuclear weapons; it is listed as a threshold state because its enrichment programme is under international scrutiny (IAEA).
